text:
Situation: Cytarabine has been on FDA's shortage list since 2021-09-24 and as of 2026-10-21 has remained listed for 61 months. Corvale East holds 25 vials of the 100 mg/mL, 20 mL presentation at 2.9 vials per day, giving 8.7 days on hand. Corvale General holds 67 vials at 2.7 vials per day, giving 24.5 days on hand. Other sites hold 20 mg/mL presentations with 14.3 to 26.8 days on hand.

Why (FDA record): The product used at Corvale General and Corvale East carries NDC 25021022320, labeled by Sagent Pharmaceuticals with manufacturing at a plant identified as GLAND. GLAND corresponds to Gland Pharma Limited (FEI 3009056604). FDA inspected this plant most recently on 2019-11-01 and classified it VAI, with the classification letter dated 2019-12-10 — 693 days before FDA posted the shortage on 2021-09-24. Earlier inspections on 2013-08-05 and 2015-06-30 were also classified VAI. A more recent inspection on 2023-07-28 was classified NAI.

Our position: Supply at Corvale East is critically low for the 100 mg/mL, 20 mL vial. Corvale General can spare inventory without dropping below two weeks. Alternate manufacturers are not on FDA's shortage list today. Alternate concentrations from Gland Pharma and Hospira have prior pharmacist approvals for substitution.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 16 vials of cytarabine 100 mg/mL, 20 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East. Approval: Pharmacy Director.
2. Purchase cytarabine from Meitheal Pharmaceuticals Inc. Approval: Buyer.
3. Purchase cytarabine from Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC. Approval: Buyer.
4. Substitute cytarabine 20 mg/mL from Gland Pharma Limited (alternate NDC). Approval: Pharmacist.
5. Substitute cytarabine 20 mg/mL from Hospira, Inc. with dose and volume recalculation. Approval: Pharmacist.

Not recommended: No action; Corvale East will exhaust 100 mg/mL, 20 mL supply in under nine days.
